comments.author: pipes
comments.why: Hit home and led commenter to quit drinking
comments.text: Listening to the huberman podcast about alcohol really hit home. I knew it was bad for me, just not as bad as he explains. It's a horrific drug that most people don't even see as a drug. I am a weekend drinker and I thought that was ok. It's not. I've decided to quit completely. Last drink was 12 days ago. Fuck alcohol. (I also used to take other drugs but that was many years ago). [VIDEO] Oh and I just finished the book: alcohol explained, utterly fantastic.

comments.author: cl42
comments.why: Convinced the commenter to stop drinking
comments.text: Related: Andrew Huberman's 2-hour blog post on the negative effects of alcohol[1] convinced me to stop drinking. Once you stop drinking, it becomes so easy to see just how much alcohol pervades popular culture. People drink constantly on TV. People pressure you to drink in social situations, too. Unfortunately, it often feels like you need a 'good reason' to stop drinking or alternatively admit you were an alcoholic. It's really unfortunate and ... silly? Reddit's "stopdrinking" subreddit is also really good[2] if you are struggling with this. [1] [VIDEO] [2] [LINK]

comments.author: softwaredoug
comments.story: SF's Anchor Brewing Company shutting down after 127 years
comments.why: Great Huberman episode on alcohol's health effects
comments.text: The pandemic has triggered / accelarated a lot of trends One trend I wonder about is cutting back on drinking. From a health perspective, I see more and more health officials loudly saying no healthy amount of alcohol[1]. It's simply poison. Not that I'm aggressively for any kind of prohibition, and don't very rarely drink, but I wonder if we'll see increased awareness and more people just deciding not to drink as much anymore. With this awareness, and the "modest amount of alcohol are actually healthy" claims debunked[2], maybe the hipster / wealthy / yuppy crowd will turn more and more away from the many many microbreweries / wineries that have cropped up in the last few decades. 1 - [LINK] Huberman has a great episode too - [VIDEO] 2 - [LINK] [LINK]

comments.text: It doesn't specify the actual ingredients. The "grapes" bit makes me think perhaps resveratrol? Dihydromyricetin is touted as being protective before and after drinking. It appears to have other benefits as well. I've now become a big fan and follower of Andrew Huberman and a recent podcast has helped sway me to effectively give up alcohol (I was already trending in that direction): [VIDEO] My one remaining active vice is Kratom and I'm pretty comfortable with my relationship with it, considering the value it gives in managing chronic pain. Obviously different strokes for different folks.

comments.author: guiambros
comments.story: Ask HN: How did you stop drinking?
comments.why: Comprehensive explanation of alcohol's effects on body and brain
comments.text: What helped me eliminate almost entirely was understanding the impact it has on the body and the brain. More than " it's bad for your health ", it helped me understand why it's bad. Even the allegedly harmless " a glass of red wine a day is good for your health " (spoiler: no). There are many sources, but I recently saw this one from Dr. Andrew Huberman, which seemed more comprehensive than a lot of what I've read before. [1] What Alcohol Does to Your Body, Brain & Health - [VIDEO]
